title: GPU admission controller and tenancy-banding for graceful noisy-neighbor mitigation
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement an admission controller and tenancy-banding system for Dedicated GPU capacity that enforces throughput guarantees while reducing noisy-neighbor impact. The goal is to allow per-tenant throughput contracts to be honored under load, provide graceful degradation for low-priority tenants, and automatically detect and mitigate noisy workloads without manual intervention.
background: Current dedicated fleet struggles when a small set of tenants repeatedly generate pathological patterns that cause KV cache thrashing and GPU memory pressure. Existing soft quotas and crude eviction heuristics (based on total GPU time) are insufficient for tail-latency sensitive customers. We need a runbook-driven admission + banding layer that combines admission tokens, tenant bands (SLO/priority buckets), and an eviction scoring function that includes cache footprint, request QPS, recent latency spikes, and per-tenant token debt.
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller runs on dedicated nodes and rejects or delays requests according to band-specific token buckets
Tenants are classified into at least three bands (Guaranteed, BestEffort, Opportunistic) and banding can be changed on-the-fly via Console/Config API
Eviction scoring for noisy-neighbor detection incorporates KV cache delta, GPU mem pressure, and 95th/99th latency spikes
Canary rollout demonstrated on 10% of dedicated fleet with no customer-facing SLO regressions for Guaranteed tenants
Dashboard shows per-tenant token usage, band transitions, eviction events, and correlation with latency regressions
Automated tests validate token bucket fairness, preemption handoff, and soft-grace-period enforcement
decisions: Use three bands by default: Guaranteed (SLA-backed), BestEffort (soft quotas, burst credits), Opportunistic (preemptible).
Admission tokens implemented as per-tenant leaky token buckets with separate burst and steady rates; tokens are replenished from tenant commitments and optional burst credits.
Eviction scoring will be additive: base_score = alpha * normalized_gpu_mem + beta * kv_cache_delta + gamma * latency_spike_score + delta * token_debt.
Preemption will prefer draining Opportunistic tasks first, then BestEffort; Guaranteed tasks will only be preempted under emergency circuit-breaker conditions with explicit approval.

Noisy-neighbor classifier (ML-light): run a lightweight anomaly detector on per-tenant time series (KV miss rate, cache evictions, GPU sm utilization) and raise a mitigation flag if anomaly score > threshold.
Default hard quota enforcement will include a short grace period (configurable, default 30s) to smooth bursty legitimate traffic before eviction.
Expose band assignment and token config in Console and via the management API for programmatic overrides and scheduled promotions/demotions.

implementation_notes: Admission controller will be a lightweight sidecar that intercepts requests at the node ingress and consults a banding table cached from control-plane.
Banding table is TTL-cached and updated from control-plane; changes propagate within 5s for scheduled promotions/demotions.
Token accounting stored in Redis-like in-cluster store with per-node shard to avoid global hot spots; local caches for read path to avoid tail latency.
Eviction scoring agent computes features every 1s window and emits events to orchestrator which coordinates graceful preemption (drain then kill if needed).
Client SDKs will receive structured 429 responses with retry-after and band metadata to enable exponential backoff and user-visible messaging.
test_plan: Unit tests for token bucket logic including edge cases (wrap-around, bursts, simultaneous replenish).
Integration tests that replay historical tenant traffic with injected noisy workloads and verify Guaranteed tenants maintain SLOs.
Canary run: 7-day run on 10% capacity with automated SLO checks and automated rollback if Guaranteed 99th latency worsens by >10%.
Chaos scenario tests: simultaneous node failures + noisy tenant to validate preemption and graceful degradation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): deploy to staging and run replay harness for 72h.
Phase 2 (canary): enable on 10% dedicated fleet; monitor 72h then 7-day window.
Phase 3 (gradual): expand canary to 33%, then 66%, then full rollout over 3 weeks with gating on dashboards.
Rollback knobs: global disable flag, per-node bypass via node-annotation, and forced-demote for misclassified tenants.
risks: Misclassification: legitimate bursty tenants could be demoted and suffer unnecessary throttling; mitigated via grace periods and manual overrides.
State divergence: banding table cache might lag under control-plane stress; mitigated with conservative TTL and fallback to BestEffort behavior.
Performance overhead: sidecar admission and eviction scoring must not add >1ms median latency on steady path; optimized C++ hot path considered if needed.
Operational complexity: new metrics and dashboards increase SRE burden; include runbooks and automated alerts to reduce toil.
